amendment.text: Oklahoma City does not change the toilet-count table. Its supplement to the 2018 International Building Code rewrites one exception to the rule on separate men's and women's rooms: a non-assembly space with 75 occupants or fewer, where no food or drink is served for on-site consumption and only one toilet is required, needs no separate rooms. In the supplement this text is in black, the colour used for city amendments (state amendments are in red). The 2018 supplement's other Chapter 29 items are a scope sentence (2901.1), the state's exception for unoccupied buildings (2902.1) and the state's directional-sign rule (2902.4.1). The city's 2018 plumbing supplement amends only Section 403.4.1 (directional signs) in Chapter 4. Whether the 75-occupant exception carries over to the state's 2024 edition is not stated on any page read: the 2024 state rule has no such exception (its exceptions are 15 or fewer in total, 25 or fewer in a business occupancy, 100 or fewer in a store).
amendment.quote: Section [P] 2902.2 Exception #4 is amended to read as follows: 4. Separate facilities are not required in non-assembly occupancies with a total occupant load of 75 or less where no food or beverage is served for on-site consumption and where only one water closet is required by Table 2902.1 and the International Plumbing Code® (IPC®) as adopted by The City of Oklahoma City.

fixtures.worked_examples_note: Not redone: the amendment changes when separate rooms are required, not how many toilets. The state pack's counts at 50, 100, 200 and 400 occupants stand. The table ratios for office, restaurant and school and the urinal shares are the same in the 2018 and 2024 editions as the state pack records them.

permit.exempt_list_quote: City amendment (2018 IBC supplement): "Section 105.2 is amended to delete numbered exemptions 1, 2, 4 and 10 under Building, and to delete exemptions titled Electrical, Gas, Mechanical and Plumbing." Base list, 2018 International Building Code Section 105.2, Building, items the city keeps (3, 5 to 9, 11 to 13): "Oil derricks. [...] Water tanks supported directly on grade if the capacity is not greater than 5,000 gallons (18 925 L) and the ratio of height to diameter or width is not greater than 2:1. Sidewalks and driveways not more than 30 inches (762 mm) above adjacent grade, and not over any basement or story below and are not part of an accessible route. Painting, papering, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, counter tops and similar finish work. Temporary motion picture, television and theater stage sets and scenery. Prefabricated swimming pools accessory to a Group R-3 occupancy that are less than 24 inches (610 mm) deep, are not greater than 5,000 gallons (18 925 L) and are installed entirely above ground. [...] Swings and other playground equipment accessory to detached one- and two-family dwellings. Window awnings in Group R-3 and U occupancies, supported by an exterior wall that do not project more than 54 inches (1372 mm) from the exterior wall and do not require additional support. Nonfixed and movable fixtures, cases, racks, counters and partitions not over 5 feet 9 inches (1753 mm) in height."
permit.city_page_quote: Permits are required when you construct, alter, repair, enlarge, move or demolish any primary or accessory structure.
permit.partitions_named_note: The list names 'partitions' only as 'nonfixed and movable [...] partitions not over 5 feet 9 inches'. Toilet partitions are not named. The same wording is in the 2024 edition's Section 105.2 (https://up.codes/viewer/oklahoma/ibc-2024/chapter/1/scope-and-administration). The city's commercial permit checklist lists 'install' among scopes of work and names no exempt work.

restrooms_city.quote: [P] 2902.4.1 Directional signage. Directional signage indicating the route to the required public toilet facilities in group A, B, I, M, and R-1 occupancies shall be posted in a lobby, corridor, aisle, or similar space, such that the sign can be readily seen from the main entrance to the building or tenant space.
restrooms_city.note: No Oklahoma City rule on single-user restroom signs or shared all-gender rooms was found: the city's 2018 building and plumbing supplements hold none (the only sign text is the state's directional-sign amendment, quoted), and one web search returned state law only. The Municipal Code was not read (Municode). This is 'none found', not 'none exists'.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Oklahoma City job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material and see the rules Oklahoma City enforces.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Oklahoma City offices, schools, state buildings and distribution centers, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Oklahoma's building rules set the number of toilets by how many people use the building. Oklahoma City's own amendments leave those numbers as the state writes them. The table below shows what that means.
extra_rule_bullets: - **Which rules apply:** Oklahoma brought in new statewide building and plumbing rules on September 14, 2026. Oklahoma City's list of adopted codes still shows the earlier ones, with the city's own amendments. Ask the city's Development Center Plan Review (405-297-2525) which set your project is reviewed under.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Oklahoma City requires a permit to construct, alter or repair a structure. Its list of work that needs no building permit includes painting, papering, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, counter tops and similar finish work, and movable partitions up to 5 feet 9 inches high that aren't fixed in place. The list doesn't name toilet partitions. Ask the city's Development Center Plan Review (405-297-2525) whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.confirm_office: the City of Oklahoma City Development Center
page.stalls_after: These are the minimums for the whole building, and at least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible. Oklahoma City's amendments to the earlier rules add one exception: a space that isn't used for assembly, holds 75 people or fewer, serves no food or drink on site and needs only one toilet doesn't need separate men's and women's rooms. The city's list of adopted codes shows no amendments to the new state rules, so ask Plan Review whether that exception applies to your project. Where a shared room is built for all genders, the count is worked out on everyone in the building instead of on each half.
page.install_rule: Oklahoma City registers contractors through its Business Licensing office. The city's registration page marks the building contractor registration as residential only, so ask Business Licensing (405-297-2606) whether your installer needs to register for a commercial job. Oklahoma has no state license for general construction or most specialty installers: the state licenses plumbing, electrical, mechanical and roofing work only. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: Oklahoma has no state license for partition installers, and Oklahoma City's Business Licensing office can tell you whether the contractor needs a city registration.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** Oklahoma has no state wage law for public jobs, so a set wage applies only on federally funded projects, under federal law. For a carpenter on building work in Oklahoma County that rate is $16.61 an hour plus $3.00 in benefits.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 8.625% in Oklahoma City: 4.5% state and 4.125% city. Oklahoma County adds no sales tax. The parts of the city in Canadian and Cleveland counties also pay a county tax.
page.buyers_extra: - **State agencies and public buildings:** one material and one hardware standard across many buildings, with heavy-duty hardware for restrooms that serve the public all day.

page.official_names: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design; ICC A117.1-2017 with Supplement 1, through Chapter 11 of the 2024 International Building Code with Oklahoma amendments (OAC 748:20-2, statewide minimum since September 14, 2026); 2024 International Plumbing Code with Oklahoma amendments (OAC 748:20-16); on the City of Oklahoma City's list of adopted codes, the 2018 International Building Code and 2018 International Plumbing Code with city and state amendments, administered by the Development Services Department under Chapters 12 and 42 of the Oklahoma City Municipal Code, 2020; NFPA 286 for HDPE.
notes: To confirm by phone before launch: which edition Oklahoma City reviews commercial plans under since September 14, 2026 (its adopted-codes page lists the 2018 editions and 2018 supplements; the state's 2024 editions are the statewide minimum), and whether the city's 75-occupant exception to separate men's and women's rooms still applies (Development Center Plan Review, 405-297-2525). If the city confirms the 2024 editions, drop the 'Which rules apply' bullet and the exception sentences under the table.

The wheelchair-access, Oklahoma extras and fire-safety bullets come from the state's 2024 rules. If the city still reviews under its 2018 list, the grab bar, toe clearance and turning circle points need rechecking against the 2018 edition's accessibility standard.

To confirm by phone: whether replacing or adding anchored toilet partitions in an existing commercial restroom needs an Oklahoma City building permit (Plan Review, 405-297-2525). The exempt list was read as the 2018 model text on UpCodes with the city's deletions applied; Chapter 12 of the Municipal Code (Sections 12-67 to 12-71, permits) was not read because Municode blocks automated access.

okc.gov blocks curl (403). Its pages were read through WebFetch, which summarises: check the adopted-codes list, the permit sentence and the contractor registration wording in a browser. The city's PDF supplements, the Tax Commission files and sam.gov were read directly.

The local-rules entry (2026-11-03) says every contractor must register with the city. That sentence is not on the city's current Contractor Registration page, which marks building contractor registration 'Residential Only', and the old URL no longer resolves. The installation paragraph asks the buyer to check with Business Licensing (405-297-2606); update the local-rules entry and the installer page after a call.
No Oklahoma City rule on restroom signs or all-gender rooms was found, so the restroom bullet is the state's. The Municipal Code was not searched.
Sales tax: 8.625% is the rate for the part of the city in Oklahoma County, which includes downtown. The Tax Commission's charts show no change through March 2027.
The public-jobs rate is the general carpenter line of the federal determination, a 2012 survey rate; carpenters doing form work have a higher union rate ($27.79 plus $10.05).
The four building types in the lead and the buyers bullet on state agencies are editorial, not sourced.
